newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BT options kept busy as shares drop.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BT options kept busy as shares drop.

text.p: UK stock options traders delved into British Telecommuncations options following a plunge in the underlying stock on Friday, dealers said.

The main deals were from traders buying call options expecting the share price to bounce. One such deal was the purchase of 500 August 500 calls at 3p, another was to buy 500 November 500 calls at 10p.
Stock market investors had taken fright in BT shares following a profits warning from America's MCI Communications Corp which could hurt BT since the two companies are set to merge.
By 1255 GMT, just under 4,000 options contracts had been traded in BT while BT shares had tumbled 50p to 427-1/2p.
The main deals in electronics group General Electric Co were from sellers of call options ahead of the stock going ex-dividend by 9.89p on Monday.
One trader sold 700 August 360 calls in GEC at 14p. The shares raced up 16-1/2p to 376p.

Options in retailing groups were also busy as underlying shares led the market higher. In Marks & Spencer the chief trade was a long straddle established by buying 250 October 600 calls and puts at 13p and 47p each.
Increased implied volatility of M&S shares will make the straddle profitable. M&S shares gained 2-1/2p to 558p.
Over in index options, some traders were active tidying up positions in the July series which expire on July 18.
Other large deals were volatility trades and one such deal was a crossed trade in which a put spread in FTSE options was hedged by an opposite position in September futures.
It involved trading 1,000 July 4625/4825 puts for a net amount of 55p against futures at 4820. By 1255 GMT, September futures were up 34 at 4812.
